correctness.rationale: The entire 5-dimensional Lie algebra is generated iff its 4-dimensional central quotient is generated: lifting the two independent simple-root directions and bracketing gives the missing highest-root direction. In the quotient, two weights have determinant three, so outside characteristic three they yield separate rank-two tests; in characteristic three they coalesce and require a joint rank-three test. Multiplication of exact finite-field rank probabilities yields both formulas. Exhaustive (q,k)=(2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(3,2) computations and independent seeded checks over prime fields and F4 corroborate without being used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact generation law solves the natural all-prime-power all-k random generation problem for the rank-two Borel of sl3, identifying a genuine jump from two required generators to three in characteristic three. That jump follows from coalescence of simple-root torus weights, connects directly to recent characteristic-dependent random-generation results for sl_n, and is not obtained by a trivial numeric substitution into an existing formula. The theorem supplies a structural rank criterion and exact finite-field probabilities that may serve as a baseline for higher-rank Borel generation.
